newsitem.title: UK: Ireland seeks compensation for "green' rate change.
newsitem.headline: Ireland seeks compensation for "green' rate change.

text.p: Ireland is seeking compensation for its farmers for loss of income caused by a revaluation in the punt green rate due to take effect Saturday, an Irish farm ministry spokesman said.
"Agriculture minister Ivan Yates is in touch with the EU Commission in relation to calculation of the losses and the level of compensation to be paid," the spokesman said.
"It is expected to be over 40 million Irish punts," he said, adding that Yates has asked the Commission to come forward as soon as possible with proposals.

The minister would consult with farmers' groups to work out how compensation would be distributed. The spokesman noted that compensation had been paid to other European Union member states in similar circumstances.

"Obviously it will affect returns in a negative sense," a spokesman for one of those groups, the Irish Co-operative Organisation Society, said. "It extends the impact of currency markets into the supported market," he said, referring primarily to intervention buying-in.
The ICOS spokesman expected an overall four percent fall in returns. "There is provision for compensation and we would expect that to be put in place," he said.
The green rate used for the punt is to be revalued to 0.778173 per ECU with effect from Saturday from its current level of 0.812908.
So-called "green' rates are used in EU farm policy to convert subsidies, levies and institutional prices set in Ecus into national currencies. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
